data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of non-experts following an explicit checklist is more reliable than a single expert for verifiable tasks because it replaces the expert's 'compressed' intuition\u2014which is prone to premature closure\u2014with a distributed, transparent audit of the problem space.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checklist is incomplete or contains critical gaps that only expert intuition can bridge.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel suffers from groupthink, leading to collective blind spots that override the checklist's intent.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist acts as a cognitive scaffolding that forces the exploration of all necessary conditions (preventing 'premature closure'), while the panel structure provides redundant verification of each condition, transforming the task from a high-stakes 'leap of intuition' into a series of low-stakes binary verifications.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
